I purchased this Walmart Branded Gaming Laptop (Overpowered OP-LP2) on April 1, 2019. I use this laptop normally for classes and work at a desk. Recently, I noticed the touchpad begin to bulge upwards and stopped functioning. I then looked inside the laptop and saw the battery was very swollen (please see attached pictures). I have previously owned 3 laptops and NONE of them have ever had their batteries swell. This Overpowered Laptop battery should not have swollen in such a short amount of time. According to [REDACTED], the electrolytes in this battery are degraded and shorting. This means these batteries are on a thermal runaway which can lead to a fire or an explosion. I can no longer take this laptop on flights because it will put all the other passengers at risk. This is a dangerous defective battery. When an [REDACTED] or [REDACTED] has a swollen battery in such a short about of time, [REDACTED] will replace the device immediately regardless if the device is out of warranty. In fact, [REDACTED] got sued in 2021 over swollen batteries. Even if my laptop battery was replaced, there may be internal hardware damage from the swollen battery.

For weeks I kept calling Walmart for a resolution. But Walmart just kept transferring me back and forth between different departments or said they would get back to me. Walmart later gave me the phone numbers to the customer support team they setup for this Walmart branded laptop, and their supplier (E&S Enterprises), both of whom never picked up the phone after numerous calls I made for days. There was no one I could reach out to for a solution. Walmart allowed these suppliers do as they please without any accountability or repercussion, even if they produce defective batteries that can harm the consumer. The Walmart rep [REDACTED] from the Walmart Customer Care Team falsely said this Overpowered laptop is not a Walmart Brand Laptop. This is false since Walmart did launch this line of gaming laptops making it their brand:

But after a few years in the gaming computer industry, Walmart failed and left us customers to fend for ourselves with hazardous batteries.

I am probably the first customer of this Overpowered laptop to report this to Walmart since I was proactive enough to check the battery after seeing the touchpad bulge upwards and stop functioning. But what about the other customers who are still using this laptop with a swollen battery since it has been just 3 years? If they take this battery on an airplane, they will put all the other passengers at risk since swollen laptop batteries can catch fire or explode. If this happens Walmart will be very liable now that they know about this defect from my many emails and phone calls where nothing got done. Walmart is clearly not trying to protect their customers after learning from me they sold defective dangerous batteries to consumers. This should be investigated to determine if Walmart should recall their Overpowered Gaming Laptops.

incident_description:
On Tuesday February 26, 2019 at 9am I was sitting in my backyard when I heard a loud pop and spark like noises.I turned to look in the direction of that noise and saw flames coming from the side of my house where my AC unit was located.
I grabbed my hose and put out the fire only to learn that the fire was started by the Supco 150 power surge protector.
While I waited for my AC company to come check this out the fire started up again. At this point I called 911.
Needless to say if I had not been home or if this happened in the middle of the night this could have ended in tragedy.

My AC technician told me and I quote I have installed thousands of these devices and yours is the third fire I have seen.
It scares me to think how long before the thousands he has installed catch on fire.

I came to learn that UL had issued a warning on this product in a public notice on July 29, 2016.
It saddens me to think that this product is still in use and can still be purchased on E-Bay.

If you Google- supco surge protector fire- you will see more accounts of this product catching fire.

There should be an immediate recall on this product.
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by a faulty surge protector, with no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
14 year-old boy was racing in a motorcross ATV event wearing a helmet mounted Contour camera on a Kinetic racing helmet.  During the race he collides with other races and crashes.  Video from the camera appears to show him flipping over the handlebars and striking the left side of his head on the ground.   The camera is also mounted to the left side of the helmet.  The video appears to show the camera breaking off the helmet and spinning into the grass after the impact with the ground.   He is unresponsive when first responders arrive.  Resuscitation is not successful and he is pronounced dead.

I performed the autopsy.  There was a focal depressed skull fracture of the left side of the skull that was the most significant injury on the body.  The appearance of the depression suggests that the head struck an object that was protruding off the ground, such as a large rock or the cylinder of the camera.  A large rock seems unlikely given that this is a motorcross racing track.  The left side of the helmet is fractured.   The camera is cylindrical shaped and was mounted to the left side of the helmet via a plastic mount.   Based on the video, the point of impact appeared to be at the camera mount site.   I know that these cameras are designed to break off the helmet with relatively minor impact as a safety mechanism.  However, in this case, the camera may have broken off only partially, or in such a way that the front of the camera turned inward toward the head, and became trapped between the head and the ground, such that when the head struck the ground, it also struck the protruding camera, resulting in the fatal depressed skull fracture.
justification: The incident resulted in a fatal injury due to a depressed skull fracture, likely caused by the camera mount during the crash.

incident_description: HidrateSpark is a Bluetooth-connected smart water bottle that reminds one to drink water through a smartphone-connected app.  The bottle reads the water level and calculates your water intake.  The charging cable provided does not have overcurrent or short circuit protection and is connected to the device using a magnetic connector with EXPOSED terminals.  Because it is magnetic, the connector is attracted to metal objects.  In the event that the terminals come in contact with exposed metal, an electrical connection is made and the connector then shorts the 5v power supply.  I had a bottle charging on my desk and disconnected it.  The cable came in contact with some exposed metal near my worksurface causing the power supply (phone charger to get extremely hot.  It happed again when plugged into a USB hub causing it to shut down the hub and all of the USB components on my computer including my mouse and keyboard.  Cables can be contructed with simple short circuit protection with the simple addition of a Polyfuse Resttable fuse that will disconnect the circuit due to overcurrent and reset once the fault is removed.
justification: The incident describes a short circuit causing overheating and equipment shutdown, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: December 24th 2011, while getting ready for a Christmas Eve party I was in my bathroom downstairs while my girlfriend was upstairs finishing getting ready in my room.  The multi-outlet surge protector was plugged into an outlet in my bedroom upstairs.  The wall outlet (top) had a controller (remote on/off switch) receiver plugged in with two Christmas lights in series.  While the bottom outlet had the surge protector plugged in with three items plugged in at the time; a plasma TV, the cable box, and my girlfriends hair straightener.  Typically only the TV and cable box are plugged into the surge protector, the top outlet usually will have one light plugged into the controller receiver.  While I was downstairs getting ready I heard my girlfriend call my name, I started heading up the stairs when I heard her call my name again except with more urgency so I ran.  By the time I reached the top of the stairs smoke was filling the room and I saw my girlfriend standing over the surge protector while it was on fire.  Fire was coming from the open outlets and had actually melted through the bottom.  I picked the item up, shaking it and blowing it out, then unplugged the item from the wall.  There was still power in the room, the circuit was not broken.  My girlfriend said she had the hair straightener plugged in with no issues, when she turned it on the surge protector started crackling and making buzzing sounds as well as sparks being seen inside the unit, spurring her first cry for help.  After she tried to unplug the hair straightener the unit caught fire causing her to scream for my help, I then ran up the stairs and put the fire out.  The room was filled with black smoke and burn marks were on the wood floor.  The surge protector appears fine on top but actually has a hole melted through the bottom.  Once I cleaned up the black marks on the floor all that was left were two dime size burn holes in the wooden floor.  The hair straightener appears to work although the plug was a little blackened by the fire.  The tv and cable box seem to work fine, after I replaced the outlet in the wall and hooked up a new surge protector I plugged both back in and they turned on without issue.  The only major damage was the burn marks in the floor, no injuries happened in the incident.
justification: The incident involved a fire and property damage but no injuries.

incident_description:
Laptop Battery exploded and started a house fire. Report below is available: 

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Fire Investigator [REDACTED] delivered the evidence for the above loss [REDACTED]
Berkeley office on September 6, 2017. The following items, identified per chain of
possession, were collected from the residence at the above loss location:
DP-#1) HP laptop CPU and charger
DP-#1a) Laptop battery
DP-#1b) Charger and debris from fire
DP-#1c) Sprinkler head
[REDACTED] of [REDACTED] inspected the evidence on September 13, 2017. The
evidence was non-destructively examined visually and through radiographic imaging. Scene
photographs were also reviewed. Based on the non-destructive examination and the review
of scene photographs, the most likely ignition source for this fire loss is the energy released
from the HP laptop battery pack. There are several possible causes of failure of these
batteries including: manufacturing defect, overheating, overcharging (of specific cells), or
mechanical damage to the battery cells.
This brief does not intend to fully outline my investigation. At your direction, a more
detailed report will be provided. Select photographs and radiographic images are embedded
in the body of the report. Additional photographs and radiographic images will remain in my
file and will be available upon request.
[Redacted] Page Claim 2 # [REDACTED]
LABORATORY SUMMARY
DP-#1) HP Laptop CPU and Charger:
Photo 1: Photo depicting the incident laptop and charger remains from DP-#1.
This evidence item consisted of an HP Pavilion g6 laptop and HP laptop charger. The
charger exhibited directional and external damage. The wall side cord was severed just after
exiting the A/C to D/C converter box. This severed wire had beads on th e stranded copper
conductors consistent with an electrical arc suggesting that the charger was plugged into an
electrical outlet. It is unknown at this time if the other end of the charger was connected to
the laptop. A radiographic image of the charger
Photo 2 (left) and 3 (right): Photos depicting the charger remains from DP-#1.
Photo 3 shows the beaded electrical conductors on the severed wall side cord of the charger.
[Redacted] Page Claim 3 # [REDACTED]
The laptop appears to have been closed during the fire. Most of the damage is concentrated
at the battery compartment at the bottom rear of the laptop and to the left side of the screen.
Additionally, there is a section on the bottom of the laptop, remote from the battery
compartment, which appears to have peeled open from heat. There are pieces of copper foil
stuck to the bottom of the laptop which appear to have been ejected from a lithium -ion
battery. These battery ejections could have caused the peeled open section on the bottom of
the laptop. A radiogr
the laptop. The laptop batteries were not included in this evidence item.
Photo 4: Photo depicting the bottom of the incident laptop from DP-#1.
DP-#1a) Laptop Battery:
Photo 5: Photo depicting the lithium-ion battery array from evidence item DP-#1a.
This evidence item contains six 18650 sized lithium-ion batteries connected in series which
were in turn connected to a small printed circuit board. The size of this ba ttery array appears
[Redacted] Page Claim 4 # [REDACTED]
consistent with the size of the battery compartment of the laptop from DP-#1. The positive
terminal end caps from two of these batteries were missing along with a portion of their
internal contents. A radiographic image of these batteries revealed that the density of the
two batteries with the missing end caps was far less than the density of the remaining four
batteries, which confirms that a portion of the internals of those two batteries were ejected.
Photo 6: Photo depicting the missing end caps from two of lithium-ion battery array from
evidence item DP-#1a.
Image 1: Radiographic image depicting the lithium-ion battery array from evidence item DP-#1a.
Note the two batteries on the left with significantly lower density and missing end caps.
[Redacted] Page Claim 5 # [REDACTED]
DP-#1b) Charger and Debris from Fire:
Photo 7 (left) and 8 (right): Photos depicting the debris from evidence item DP-#1b.
This evidence item contained the remains of a three-conductor power cord and a various fire
debris. Upon review of the scene photographs, the power cord serviced a soldering iron that
as reportedly not plugged in at the time of the fire. Melted plastic on the distal end of the
cord suggests indeed that it was not plugged in at the time of the fire. Among the debris of
this evidence item were pieces of the laptop monitor, bits of copper foil, and other pieces
from the laptop. The pieces of copper foil are most likely part of the internal components
ejected from the lithium-ion batteries from DP-#1a.
DP-#1c) Sprinkler Head:
Photo 9: Photo depicting the sprinkler head from evidence item DP-#1c.
[Redacted] Page Claim 6 # [REDACTED]
This evidence item contained a sprinkler head. This sprinkler head appears to have activated.
The sprinkler head also exhibited signs of mechanical damage most likely caused by fire
department overhaul and/or evidence collection. This sprinkler head was rated for 160° F.
CONCLUSION
Based on a non-destructive examination of the evidence collected from this loss and the
scene photographs, the mostly likely cause of the fire in this case is a fault or failure of the
HP lithium-ion battery pack leading to the ejection of the contents of two of the battery cells
and the combustion of the HP laptop.
A search of the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) website revealed that there
are three separate recalls for HP Pavilion battery packs, two of which had been expanded in
their scope (one was expanded twice). Because of the damage to the battery pack identifying
information, it is unclear at this time if the battery pack was included in one of these recalls
or their expansions.
Recommendations:
[REDACTED] recommends performing destructive testing on the evidence collected in
this case to further refine the ignition scenario hypothesis. In addition, [REDACTED]
will be placing HP on notice of this loss and inviting them to have their own expert attend
the destructive testing.
Our assessment of this case is based on an analysis of the physical evidence and an
evaluation of all possible causes. Please do not hesitate to contact our office if you have any
questions or if we can be of further assistance.
justification: The laptop battery explosion caused a house fire, but there is no mention of injuries or fatalities in the report.

Charger was plugged into power strip with three other chargers one of which was the same Verizon model.  All had ipads or iphones connected.  All have been owned for at least a year. incident_description:
This report pertains to a product sold by Amazon in United States. It is called: "NEWDERY for Apple Watch Charger, 10000mAh Portable Charger Power Bank". It's Amazon product page is here: https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B0BZTXZZ77/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_search_asin_title?ie=UTF8&psc=1

Here is what happened. The product was bought in August, in USA where I reside. It was used sporadically in the last 2 months. 
We (my partner, our toddler son, and  I) traveled to Uruguay on September 27, 2024, and are staying until October 10.

At about 4am on October 1, while sleeping in a guest room of a family member's house,
we were woken up by a crackling hissing noise emanating from this Newdery charger (power bank). 
It was spinning around and it was on fire -- thin tongues of flame
were emanating from it. The fire resembled several firecrackers lit at once. It was emanating from the underside
of the unit and was extremely hot. It took us about 10 seconds to (sort of) put the fire out,
while the unit (on its own) was spinning around the floor, like a whirling dervish.  Finally, I used a large
pillow to extinguish the flame and then I carried (holding it between two shoes) the still glowing/hissing/crackling
carcass of the unit to the kitchen sink and immersed it in water. It continued to hiss for another 4-5 seconds.

It is an absolute miracle that the fire started with us being in the room. Otherwise, it would've burned down the entire
house where we were staying. It is also fortunate that the floor was tiled! If it was a linoleum, carpet, or wood floor,
much more damage would have been done. Another miracle is that none of us was burned, though it came close.
The damages amounted to burned sheets, a pillow, a mattress, and quite a few clothes. PLEASE NOTE that we
have photo evidence for all of this.

The entire floor where the unit burned was covered in black soot and the air stunk terribly. All 3 of us
inhaled some of that soot while putting out the fire. 

Also, when we originally went to sleep that night (4 hours before the fire, around 11pm) the unit was left *unplugged*,
meaning that it was not charging anything and it was also not being charged. It was on the floor in the middle
of the room near some of our suitcases  and clothes, but nothing was either touching it or covering it.

I tried to report this dangerous product to Amazon via its normal "product review" feature.
After I submitted a review, Amazon replied with an idiotic
form email saying that the review couldn't be accepted  because "it violated community standards"!!?

I believe it is imperative to (1) notify customers, both past and potential, about this dangerous product
and, (2) stop Amazon from peddling it to people.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing property damage but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the sporadic use and unplugged state before the incident.

incident_description:
Microsoft is apparently aware of a known issue with the original Surface Book where, after a number of years, the battery in the clipboard (screen unit that houses processor and most computing parts) begins swelling.  My particular unit indicated this is happening a few days ago.  The battery has swollen to the point that it has separated the screen from its bezel (i.e., the battery is pushing the screen from its mount).  This is a huge safety issue as a swelling battery can explode or catch fire.  Microsoft has not alerted owners of these devices to this issue and only offers repair at $599.  These units should be recalled and repaired immediately.  Microsoft lists "lifted or bulging screens" in the drop-down lists for issues about this system but does not explain that the issue is caused by the battery swelling.  When I contacted Microsoft Support, the representative explained that the unit could not be shipped in this condition because of the level of hazard presented by the battery.  

This issue can cause serious bodily harm if the battery explodes.
justification: The battery swelling poses a significant safety risk with potential for explosion or fire, which could cause serious bodily harm.

Approximately 2 weeks ago he pulled it off the wall mount and noticed that the screw and plastic area on the rear of the TV had melted.  He feels that the female part of the socket was touching the circuit board which caused this incident.

(2/18/15)The manufacturer was contacted and he was advised that someone  would contact him in a few days.  He is concerned that this TV is a fire hazard and should be reported before someone has a house fire.
justification: The TV overheated and melted, but no injury or fire occurred.

incident_description: I was rocking my baby with my foot while she was strapped into her on the floor bouncer/rocker, I notice some yellow/orange liquid on my foot from where I was rocking her, I take her out and look under her bouncer and see that a liquid is leaking from her vibration attachment. I realized it was battery acid from the battery inside. This battery was fairly new and bought recently from a dollar store the brand being e circuit . The battery had exploded and was leaking battery acid everywhere it could have been a lot worse if gone unnoticed. However trying to wash the battery acid off my foot did burn which was the only injury that occurred.

incident_description:
I received a brand new Apple iPhone 7 as a gift in December 2017. It was activated a few months later, and not long after that I started to experience burning, itching, aching pains in my forearms whenever I would hold and use this phone. If I put this phone in my pants pocket, it would cause a localized burning, itching aching pain on my leg. If the phone was turned off or set to "Airplane" mode the pains would cease to occur. Other times if I had been holding the phone for too long, the pain would linger for days after. 

The least painful way I found to use this phone was to not hold it and lay it on a flat surface, but this only proved to slightly lessen the pain. Eventually the pain escalated to the point that I made an appointment with my Physician, and I was advised to stop using this phone. I even applied bags of ice to both my forearms to alleviate the pain, but that only helped slightly. I am now scheduled to see an orthopedic specialist.

There is quite a bit of anecdotal evidence on the internet that many Apple products (i.e. Apple watches, iPads, iPhones) are causing many people physical symptoms. This is a very real problem that may be posing a great risk to Apple users and should be investigated as soon as possible.
justification: The user experienced physical pain and required medical attention, indicating an injury.

incident_description: My laptop electrocuted me several times when I made contact with the screws in the bottom of it and was using a foot spa. I can also feel the electricity on the surface of the case at all times just by running my fingers on it without any water around me at all. It also discharges it's battery even when powered completely off and must remain plugged in near constantly or the battery will die after only 3hrs of use. Recently while on a trip I had my laptop in my case and was carrying it. It completely discharged the battery within just a few hours and all day I was having my hair stand on end and had static electricity issues from it constantly discharging on me. Along with this, it "fried" it's operating system after less than a week of ownership and has had continuous issues since - something that may be caused by it constantly short circuiting or something of that nature. I am a young adult and the shock caused me to lose feeling in the hand that touched the laptop. Luckily, I wasn't trying to move the laptop or I likely would have dropped it. I also have concerns about people who have pacemakers using a product like this, as I'm not sure if it would cause life threatening issues for them to be shocked.
justification: The incident caused injury (loss of feeling in the hand) and poses a continuous risk of electric shock, indicating a moderate severity level.

Sometime later, she was able to speak with a rep. (name unknown).  The firms rep. spoke about copyright information, but the consumer was not calling about copyright concerns.  The consumer said that the rep. was unwilling to assist her further.



The consumers child asked if the brightness could be turned down on the product, because it was impacting their ability to use the product.

The consumer placed the product on her head and immediately the light inside the product impacted her eyes and caused her to have headaches for days.

She tried to call the BBB, to report this matter, but was unsuccessful.  The consumer believes that when one places the product on their head, it attacks the users eyes.
justification: The consumer experienced headaches for days due to the product's brightness, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as the issue occurred when the product was used as intended.

incident_description: General alarm for a possible structure fire. Enroute dispatch stated fire was an A/C unit on outside of house. incident_description:

incident_description:

justification: The incident caused panic, evacuation, and a public safety hazard, though no injuries were reported.
